purpose: Frozen pre-upgrade snapshot of the four quality gates per test-strategy.md §1 and §5. Every wave diffs against this baseline; pre-existing failures are recorded separately so P2+ regressions are attributable. Captured via 'npm ls --workspaces --depth=0', 'npm audit --json', 'node scripts/check-monorepo-boundaries.mjs', and the per-app CI scripts (lint/test/typecheck/build).

npm_ls.summary: Clean. No dependency-tree problems across the 5 apps and 19 active shared packages (20 total non-root workspaces, 1 _template excluded).

npm_audit.summary: 18 advisories (1 critical, 3 high, 14 moderate). The critical advisory targets vitest 2.x isolated in packages/practice-test-engine. The 3 high advisories are the installed Next.js, React Server Components, and Vite RSC plugin versions. See audit-baseline.json security_totals for the canonical breakdown.

boundary_check.summary: No monorepo boundary violations. Shared packages do not import from apps/* or convex/_generated/*. The scripts/ directory is outside the boundary-check searchIn, so audit scripts are not subject to the rule.

per_app_quality_gates.purpose: Per-app lint/test/typecheck/build status captured before any upgrade wave. Each app's CI scripts are run; results are recorded so a wave that flips a previously-green app to red is attributable.

pre_existing_failures.purpose: Failures known to exist before any upgrade wave. Any new failure introduced in a wave is an upgrade regression attributable to that wave. The label/owner/track field links back to the in-flight track so the failure is not silently dropped.
pre_existing_failures.policy: Per spec Out-of-Scope, pre-existing failures unrelated to the upgrade are not auto-fixed; they are recorded here for attribution. If a wave resolves one of these as a side effect, mark it resolved with the wave SHA.

single_root_lockfile_invariant.purpose: Cross-check the npm ls result against the filesystem: exactly one package-lock.json at the repo root, zero nested. See also lockfile-inventory.json (AC7, FR10).

wave_attribution_rules: A failure introduced in wave W is an upgrade regression; fix or revert before moving to W+1.
A failure that exists in this baseline and persists after a wave is NOT a wave regression; it remains in pre_existing_failures.
If a wave resolves a pre-existing failure, the failure row is moved out of pre_existing_failures and tagged with the wave SHA.
